independent_checks.py: ROMAN_OK (17 counts, 243 shift, 243 difference, four full graph enumerations)
correctness.rationale: The 9-symbol column model implements exactly one 2-neighbor for each zero and positive-neighbor support for each nonzero label. The 81-state min-plus recursion checked all 81 shift identities at each r=3,4,5 and all 81 fourth-difference identities at those phases. Fixed 3-step optimal-transition matrices extend the finite identities inductively to all lengths; fourth finite differences enforce polynomial counts; four terminal values interpolate each residue class. Independently rebuilt enumerator reproduced 17 terminal counts, 243 shift and 243 count identities, and independently enumerated graph labels for n=2..5. No inference of an infinite formula from a short scan alone.
residual_risks: Finite independent calculations do not establish untested infinite cases; unrestricted conclusions rest on proof lemmas.

evidence: 2022 theorem handles a different perfect Roman parameter on larger Cartesian grids, a bound rather than every minimum labeling. Resultary findings concern complete multipartite graphs, not path-ladder products.

value.rationale: A canonical infinite family of width-2 graphs has a complete optimization and all-minimizer enumeration. Distinct minimum labelings are natural graph-domination objects; polynomial residue counts, unique n multiple-of-three minimizers, and nontrivial finite-state induction are mathematically informative rather than a renamed existing bound.
residual_risks: Scope is restricted to ladders n>=2; no result on wider Cartesian grids.

final_claim: For P2 square Pn, n>=2: minimum weight 2n-2 floor(n/3); M_n is 1 (n=3q), q+1 (n=3q+1), or 13+9q(q+3)/2 (n=3q+2), with n=2 separately included.
limitations: Scope is restricted to ladders n>=2; no result on wider Cartesian grids.
